title: Size Computation Overflow in Container Allocation
platform_conditions: C++11 and later on any conforming toolchain; signed overflow in the size computation is undefined behavior, unsigned wraps silently
security_mechanism: Container capacity math runs in the same machine integers as C: `user_n * sizeof(int)` in size_t wraps modulo 2^64 (or 2^32), so two large attacker values produce a small product and reserve()/resize()/new[] succeed with a fraction of the requested storage. Subsequent indexed writes counted with the original n then run past the small allocation. Mixed-width arithmetic makes it worse: an int count converted to size_t sign-extends a negative value into a near-2^64 number, and a reserve() that throws bad_alloc on one platform silently wraps on another where size_t is narrower.

source_sink_clues.source: Counts, element counts, or message lengths taken from protocol fields and request bodies (e.g. an item-count header followed by the items).
source_sink_clues.sink: vector::reserve/resize, new T[n], make_unique<T[]>(n), or any allocator call whose argument is a product or sum of attacker values

tracking_guards: Check that the count is bounded by an explicit protocol maximum before any arithmetic, that the multiplication uses a checked builtin (__builtin_mul_overflow) or a pre-division test (n > SIZE_MAX / sizeof(T)), and that the result stays in size_t throughout with no intermediate int conversions.
not_candidate_when: The count is validated to a small fixed maximum before allocation, the element size and count are compile-time constants with a provably in-range product, or the allocation feeds an offline tool whose inputs no external party controls.
